system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## 0. Preliminary point: the "[STANDARD]" labels and "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller's package says that clauses marked [STANDARD] "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that the Buyer "has already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." **We should not proceed on that basis.**

- Nothing in our playbook or authority process records any such clearance. Under playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3, a counterparty's description of a clause as agreed, standard or cleared does not make it so.
- Almost every [STANDARD] item departs from our playbook, several of them materially.
- The only clause labelled differently is none at all. Nothing is marked [OPEN], so the note would in effect remove the whole package from review.

I have reviewed every clause on its merits. **Recommended response:** say expressly in our cover note that the Buyer has not accepted any clause, label or framework, and that all positions remain open until a signed agreement exists.

The Disclosure Letter itself is fairly candid (items 2–11 largely confirm our concerns). It also speaks as at **22 September 2026**, about six weeks ago. Every factual position below should be refreshed against the current DD record before we rely on it.

---

## 1. Limitation package

### 1.1 General cap: Clause 12.1 (Seller: 20% / AUD 4.8m)
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Issue:** 20% matches our conditional fallback. That fallback is usable **only** with prior written authority from Amelia Frost that identifies this draft, and no such authority exists. A number matching a fallback does not clear it.
- **Push back:** Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m. If the team wants to consider 20%, escalate to Amelia Frost for written authority referencing SPA-003 / this Seller Update. Even then, 20% should only be traded for movement elsewhere, such as thresholds, Bluefen and Riverlark.

### 1.2 Thresholds: Clause 12.2 (Seller: AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k basket, excess only)
- **Playbook:** AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 basket; first-dollar recovery once exceeded.
- **Issue:** The de minimis is 5x ours and the basket is 5x ours. The "excess only" (deductible) structure permanently strips the first AUD 250k of every valid claim. Combined with a 20% cap, this sharply erodes protection on a AUD 24m deal.
- **Push back:** Reject. Restore 5k / 50k / tipping basket. Confirm that the thresholds do not apply to Title/Fundamental, Tax, specific indemnities, payment covenants or fraud.

### 1.3 Time limits and "all Claims" override: Clauses 12.3 / 13 (Seller: 18 months)
- **Playbook:** 24 months for general claims. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval, and none has been given.
- **Hidden override:** The proposal that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" makes the general regime the default for every category. That includes Title, Tax, IP, indemnities, covenants and potentially fraud. This is exactly the hidden general-regime override the playbook prohibits.
- **Push back:** Counter at 24 months. Delete the default-application language. Replace it with an express structure in which each category (General / Fundamental-Title / Tax / IP / specific indemnities / payment and covenant claims / fraud) has its own stated regime, and general limitations apply **only** to General Warranty Claims.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title (Seller: same caps and time limits as general)
- **Playbook:** separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Issue:** Capping title at AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m share purchase means we could pay full price for shares the Seller cannot deliver and recover only 20%. "Administrative simplicity" is not a justification.
- **Push back:** Reject outright. This is a core position and not a trading item.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance: Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 ("all Claims of any nature")
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. **No one may waive this.**
- **Issue:** "All Claims of any nature" contains no fraud carve-out. It would purport to cap and time-bar fraud claims and to bar reliance-based fraud or misleading-conduct claims. Any enforceability limits under the general law or the ACL do not justify omitting an express carve-out.
- **Push back:** Non-negotiable. Insert an express carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct, by the Seller or its officers, employees or advisers, from every limitation, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clause. Also confirm that non-reliance does not cover the Warranties, the Disclosure Letter's specific disclosures or specific indemnities.

---

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge

### 2.1 General disclosure: Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2
- **Seller:** discloses everything "contained or referred to" in the whole data room (as at 22 Sept 2026), plus the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."
- **Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Issues:**
  - "Referred to" extends disclosure to documents that are not even in the data room.
  - Public-records disclosure is open-ended.
  - Combined with 8.3 (below), this would neutralise most warranties.
- **Push back:** Delete 1.1 and 1.2. Disclosure should qualify a warranty only where it is fair, specific, and sufficiently detailed to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely impact, against the specific warranty concerned. Data room documents may be referenced in specific disclosures, but only the identified content counts.

### 2.2 Non-admission: Disclosure Letter 1.4
- This is broadly acceptable as a non-admission. Clarify that it does not limit any warranty, indemnity, covenant or condition. It must also not allow the Seller to argue that, say, the Riverlark discharge or Bluefen consent is "not legally required" and so need not be delivered at Completion.

### 2.3 Buyer knowledge: Clause 8.3
- **Seller:** no claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named seller-knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. Never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Issues:**
  - The clause covers advisers' knowledge and constructive ("discoverable") knowledge.
  - It would bar claims for exactly the matters we have diligenced and are protecting through indemnities: Ironquay, DD-006, Riverlark and bonuses.
- **Push back:** Delete. Add an express statement that the Buyer's rights are not affected by any investigation or knowledge, actual, constructive or imputed. If any Seller-side "awareness" qualifier is used in the warranties, it must be limited to named individuals who have made reasonable enquiry.

---

## 3. Completion conditions and deal-critical items

### 3.1 Bluefen consent: Clauses 3 / 6.3
- **Facts (DL item 2):** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%). The contract has a change-control consent at cl 11.2 with conditions at cl 11.3. **No final written consent and no evidence that the conditions are satisfied** has been provided.
- **Seller:** reasonable endeavours, and the condition is "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent."
- **Playbook:** effective consent **and** evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer.
- **Issues:**
  - A delivered letter could be conditional, qualified or subject to unmet cl 11.3 conditions, yet still trigger satisfaction.
  - At 30% of revenue, losing Bluefen would go to price.
- **Push back:**
  - Make it a condition precedent: unconditional, effective written consent under cl 11.2, plus evidence satisfactory to the Buyer (acting reasonably) that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, or validly waived by Bluefen in writing.
  - The Seller should use all reasonable/best endeavours, with defined steps, Buyer consultation and Buyer sign-off on the consent form.
  - Only the Buyer may waive the condition, and the Buyer should have a termination right at the sunset date.
  - Add a pre-Completion warranty/covenant that no notice of termination or non-renewal has been received.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility: Clauses 2 / 7
- **Facts (DL item 3):** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding. The facility has change-control at cl 8.1 and discharge at cl 9.2. It is **not repaid** and **no discharge** is included.
- **Seller:** release "to be provided following Completion."
- **Playbook:** current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking from the lender **and** Amelia Frost approval.
- **Issues:**
  - Completing a debt-free deal while bank security remains on Company assets (and possibly the shares) is unacceptable.
  - The change of control under cl 8.1 may itself trigger default or acceleration.
  - "Approximately" AUD 3.2m is not a payout figure.
- **Push back:**
  - Require a current payout letter (with per-diem and break costs) and payment of that amount direct to Riverlark from the funds flow, deducted as Debt.
  - Require executed deeds of release, PPSR financing-change statements and ASIC charge releases (if any), in escrow at Completion.
  - Require confirmation that cl 8.1 will not be triggered before discharge.
  - Do not accept post-completion release unless Riverlark gives an irrevocable undertaking to release on receipt of the payout amount **and** Amelia Frost approves in writing.

### 3.3 Employee bonuses and funds flow
- **Facts (DL item 5):** DD-005 Completion bonuses total AUD 420,000. These are **not** in the funds flow. The position on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs is unstated.
- **Seller:** the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. In practice that means the Company pays them post-Completion on our watch, with no deduction, and the price is silently overstated.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420k plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or Seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Push back:**
  - Treat the bonuses and all associated on-costs (employer super, payroll tax, workers' comp, PAYG withholding mechanics) as Debt or Transaction Costs deducted from the price.
  - Alternatively, require the Seller to fund them into the Company at Completion, with a specific indemnity for any shortfall.
  - Do not assume a figure for on-costs; require the Seller to confirm the calculation.
  - Clarify how amounts that lapse (if continued-employment conditions fail) are treated.
- "Agreed price mechanics" is an assertion only. We have not agreed a funds flow that omits these amounts.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP: Clause 11.1
- **Facts (DL item 4):** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, but this is **not** bank-verified. No receipt or confirmatory assignment exists.
- **Seller:** the indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment and "adequate."
- **Playbook:** broaden the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180k is not independently verified either way.
- **Issue:** The real risk is not the AUD 180k. It is that the Company may not own the SOW3 IP, plus any infringement or third-party claim, loss of use and re-development cost. A payment-only indemnity does not cover that.
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to all Loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or have unrestricted rights to, the SOW3 Project Materials, or any Ironquay claim. It should sit outside the general cap, basket and knowledge bar.
  - Preserve the cure: settlement of the verified outstanding SOW3 amount at or before Completion (for example, paid from the funds flow), plus a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay as a Completion deliverable.
  - Require bank-verified confirmation of the amount actually outstanding rather than accepting AUD 180k as either correct or incorrect.

### 3.5 Export/privacy incident (DD-006): Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6
- **Facts (DL item 6):** A download link went to an unintended external address. The export covers potentially ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Access, scope and notification obligation are **not established**, and the investigation is preliminary.
- **Seller:** "not expected to be material." This is an unsupported assertion.
- **Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric loss in either direction.
- **Push back:**
  - Do not accept a materiality characterisation and do not let it qualify warranties.
  - Add covenants requiring the Seller to preserve all logs and evidence, complete the investigation diligently (with independent forensic review if appropriate), give regular written updates and access to findings, and make no regulator or individual notifications or admissions without consulting the Buyer.
  - Consider a specific indemnity for losses arising from the incident, sitting outside the general limitations.
  - We should not claim a breach occurred or price a loss figure, but we also should not accept the Seller's assurance that it is immaterial.

### 3.6 Sandbar supplier renewals (AUD 330,000)
- **Facts (DL item 8):** There are three related renewals of AUD 110k each, to be "read together for timing/scope." Whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course is **not stated**.
- **Seller:** "ordinary-course operating costs." This is an assertion. The Seller's own disclosure does not support it.
- **Playbook:** assess. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Issue:** The splitting into three equal related renewals warrants scrutiny, for example against any approval threshold or the ordinary-course covenant.
- **Push back:**
  - Request the contracts and approval records, and confirm term, termination rights, prepayment or accrual treatment, and business rationale.
  - Reserve the position on treatment (Debt, working capital or ordinary-course) pending that review.
  - Reflect the outcome in the conduct-of-business covenant.

### 3.7 Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009): DL items 7, 9
- These are not raised in the Seller Update.
- The material does not identify landlord or Mossvale consent as triggered by a share sale. Verify this against the underlying clauses rather than relying on the Seller's characterisation.
- At minimum, make the lease notification a Completion deliverable or a covenant.

---

## 4. Category integrity: Tax, IP, Title

### 4.1 Tax / IP ("settled under the general regime")
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain **OPEN**. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Push back:** Reject the "settled" characterisation. Keep Tax and IP as separate categories with their own regimes, to be negotiated. Combined with the 12.3 / 13 default override, this statement is the mechanism by which the general cap, basket and 18 months would silently capture these categories.

### 4.2 Title evidence (DD-012)
- **Facts (DL item 10):** The share register records Harbourglass as 100% holder. The Seller itself states that this "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification."
- **Playbook:** require independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is an internal source, not independent proof.
- **Push back:** Require:
  - a current ASIC company extract and historical share-issue/transfer documents;
  - original share certificates (or a lost-certificate indemnity);
  - PPSR searches against Seller and Company, with particular regard to any Riverlark security over the shares or assets;
  - the constitution and any shareholder agreements (for pre-emption or transfer restrictions and waivers);
  - Seller board resolutions authorising the sale.
- Title and capacity warranties should be on the Fundamental regime (see 1.4).

---

## 5. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | [STANDARD] / "cleared" labels | Treat as agreed | **Reject.** Nothing agreed; all open |
| 1 | General cap | 20% / 4.8m | **25% / 6.0m.** 20% only with Amelia Frost written authority (none) |
| 2 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k, excess only | **5k / 50k, first dollar** |
| 3 | General time limit | 18 months | **24 months.** 18 months needs Amelia Frost approval (none) |
| 4 | "Limitations apply to all Claims" | Default override | **Delete.** Separate express regimes per category |
| 5 | Fundamental / Title | Same as general | **100% cap, ≥6 years**, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge |
| 6 | Fraud carve-out | None | **Non-negotiable** carve-out from all limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance |
| 7 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public records | **Specific fair disclosure only** |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket, incl. advisers and "discoverable" | **Delete.** No exclusion for title, capacity, fraud or indemnities |
| 9 | Bluefen (~30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; consent-on-delivery | **CP: effective consent + evidence cl 11.3 satisfied**; stronger endeavours; Buyer-only waiver |
| 10 | Riverlark (~3.2m) | Release post-Completion | **Payout letter, direct repayment, releases at Completion.** Otherwise irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval |
| 11 | Bonuses (420k + on-costs) | Excluded from funds flow | **Line item / Debt or Seller-funded**, plus indemnity |
| 12 | Ironquay IP | Payment-only indemnity | **Broaden to IP ownership loss**; preserve SOW3 cure; verify amount |
| 13 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | **Preservation, investigation and update covenants**; no materiality assumption; consider specific indemnity |
| 14 | Sandbar (330k) | Ordinary course | **Assess**; request documents; reserve treatment |
| 15 | Tax / IP | "Settled" | **OPEN**, separate categories |
| 16 | Title | Register DD-012 | **Independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence** |

### Next steps
1. **Cover note to Seller.** State that no clause, label or framework has been accepted, and that our mark-up follows.
2. **Internal escalation.** If the team wishes to consider the 20% cap or 18-month fallbacks, or a post-completion Riverlark release, seek Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft *before* conceding anything. Until then, our positions are 25% and 24 months.
3. **DD refresh.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 Sept 2026. Request current status on:
   - Bluefen consent and cl 11.3 conditions;
   - the Riverlark payout figure;
   - the DD-006 investigation;
   - the bank-verified Ironquay balance;
   - bonus on-costs;
   - Sandbar contracts.

   Treat Seller characterisations as assertions until verified.
4. **Mark-up priorities.** Fraud carve-out, Title regime, the "all Claims" override and the disclosure/knowledge clauses come first. These are structural, and they determine whether the rest of the protections have any value.
=== END ADVICE ===
